slots.writingObjective: State as a fact about TextOS that a product change can become a proposed topic, and becomes an article only after a person accepts it.
One sentence for a search result: TextOS turns merged product changes into proposed article topics a person accepts or refuses, and publishes nothing automatically.

Open on the reader's situation: the product ships every week, the website says nothing about it, and nobody has time to translate pull requests into articles. Set up the question: can the changes themselves become the starting point, without retyping them and without losing control of what is said?
slots.buyerIntent: Can my product changes feed my articles?

slots.heading: How can I turn my product changes into articles without retyping them?
slots.writingObjective: Answer directly: a change from the repository enters TextOS by one path, is qualified by one rule and becomes content through one chain; topics are born as proposals and none is accepted without a human decision; a change becomes an article only through the same accepted brief as any other topic.
slots.buyerIntent: How can I turn my product changes into articles without retyping them?

slots.heading: What happens to a merged change
slots.writingObjective: Explain the qualification step for a non-technical reader: the author of the change declares what changed and its nature, or gives a reasoned rejection; how far the change may be talked about publicly is never left to the author but derived from what the product officially states; the step uses no language model and gives the same result when replayed on the same inputs. Say what that changes for a marketing lead.
slots.buyerIntent: Who decides what a change is worth saying?

slots.writingObjective: Caption the figure of this note in one or two factual sentences, grounded in the evidence it cites.

slots.heading: What a proposed topic is built from
slots.writingObjective: Explain the proposal step: it is deterministic, involves no language model and no paid call, and proposing twice gives the same result; only verbatim public bounds or approved profile claims enter the material the writer may use; the author's own explanation of a change explains why it was selected and never grants permission to publish it.
slots.buyerIntent: Will it repeat whatever the engineer wrote in the commit?

slots.heading: When TextOS says nothing, it says why
slots.writingObjective: Explain abstention: when the product's public status of a change cannot be established, the change is not promoted but flagged as a gap to fix in the product repository; being qualified, or even safe to mention, is never turned into acceptance or permission to publish; a topic a person refused is not proposed again for the same change.
slots.buyerIntent: What happens when a change is not publishable?

slots.heading: What stays with the person, and what this does not cover yet
slots.writingObjective: Explain that every article goes through the shared article review and a human approval and nothing is published automatically; state the current limit plainly: today the product reads only TextOS's own repository; close on what a buyer should expect from this kind of workflow, without promising dates or availability.
slots.buyerIntent: What do I still have to do?

slots.heading: What to ask any tool that writes from your changelog
slots.writingObjective: Give the buyer a short list of questions to put to any vendor, one per sentence, drawn from the mechanisms this note describes. Recommendations only, no claim about TextOS.
